arxiv-2012-03075.title: Social System Inference from Noisy Observations
arxiv-2012-03075.creator: Yanbing Mao, Naira Hovakimyan, Tarek Abdelzaher, Evangelos Theodorou
arxiv-2012-03075.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Yanbing Mao, Naira Hovakimyan, Tarek Abdelzaher, Evangelos Theodorou. This paper studies social system inference from a single trajectory of public evolving opinions, wherein observation noise leads to the statistical dependence of samples on time and coordinates. We first propose a cyber-social system that comprises individuals in a social network and a set of information sources in a cyber layer, whose opinion dynamics explicitly takes confirmation bias, novelty bias and process noise into account.

arxiv-2105-05216.title: ReflectNet - A Generative Adversarial Method for Single Image Reflection Suppression
arxiv-2105-05216.creator: Andreea Bîrhală, Ionuţ Mironică
arxiv-2105-05216.description: Abstract Taking pictures through glass windows almost always produces undesired reflections that degrade the quality of the photo. The ill-posed nature of the reflection removal problem reached the attention of many researchers for more than decades. The main challenge of this problem is the lack of real training data and the necessity of generating realistic synthetic data.

arxiv-2110-10393.title: Variable Selection in Doubly Truncated Regression
arxiv-2110-10393.creator: Ming Zheng, Chanjuan Lin, Wen Yu
arxiv-2110-10393.description: Abstract Doubly truncated data arise in many areas such as astronomy, econometrics, and medical studies. For the regression analysis with doubly truncated response variables, the existence of double truncation may bring bias for estimation as well as affect variable selection.

arxiv-2211-12766.title: One-loop tensor power spectrum from an excited scalar field during inflation
arxiv-2211-12766.creator: Atsuhisa Ota, Misao Sasaki, Yi Wang
arxiv-2211-12766.description: Abstract We present a consistent one-loop calculation for the inflationary tensor power spectrum in the presence of an excited spectator scalar field using the in-in formalism. We find that the super-horizon primordial power spectrum of the tensor mode can be scale-invariantly enhanced or reduced by the loop effects of a subhorizon scalar field.

arxiv-2303-11994.title: Higher-order Organization in the Human Brain from Matrix-Based Rényi’s Entropy
arxiv-2303-11994.creator: Qiang Li \sthanks Corresponding author: qiang.li@uv.es, Student Member, IEEE, Shujian Yu \sthanks Corresponding author: s.yu3@vu.nl, Kristoffer H Madsen, Vince D Calhoun, Armin Iraji
arxiv-2303-11994.description: Abstract Pairwise metrics are often employed to estimate statistical dependencies between brain regions, however they do not capture higher-order information interactions. It is critical to explore higher-order interactions that go beyond paired brain areas in order to better understand information processing in the human brain.

arxiv-2402-14951.title: In-Context Learning of a Linear Transformer Block: Benefits of the MLP Component and One-Step GD Initialization
arxiv-2402-14951.creator: Ruiqi Zhang, Jingfeng Wu, Peter L. Bartlett
arxiv-2402-14951.description: Abstract We study the in-context learning (ICL) ability of a Linear Transformer Block (LTB) that combines a linear attention component and a linear multi-layer perceptron (MLP) component. For ICL of linear regression with a Gaussian prior and a non-zero mean , we show that LTB can achieve nearly Bayes optimal ICL risk.

arxiv-2405-06483.title: LyS at SemEval-2024 Task 3: An Early Prototype for End-to-End Multimodal Emotion Linking as Graph-Based Parsing
arxiv-2405-06483.creator: Ana Ezquerro, David Vilares
arxiv-2405-06483.description: Abstract This paper describes our participation in SemEval 2024 Task 3, which focused on Multimodal Emotion Cause Analysis in Conversations. We developed an early prototype for an end-to-end system that uses graph-based methods from dependency parsing to identify causal emotion relations in multi-party conversations.

arxiv-2505-14445.title: Secants, Socles and Stability
arxiv-2505-14445.creator: Aaron Bertram
arxiv-2505-14445.description: Abstract 1. Introduction Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and: S_{\bullet}=k[x_{0},...,x_{n}]_{\bullet} be the polynomial ring, graded by degree. The geometry of the secants to: {\mathbb{P}}(S_{1})=:{\mathbb{P}}^{n}\hookrightarrow{\mathbb{P}}^{n}_{d}:={\mathbb{P}}(S_{d}) (the “ d -uple embeddings”) is a polynomial version of the Waring problem for natural numbers [ War ] .

plos-pone-0003258.creator: Amelia Cimmino, Rosanna Capasso, Fabbri Muller et al.
plos-pone-0003258.description: PLOS ONE research article. Natural proteins undergo in vivo spontaneous post-biosynthetic deamidation of specific asparagine residues with isoaspartyl formation. Deamidated-isomerized molecules are both structurally and functionally altered. The enzyme isoaspartyl protein carboxyl- O -methyltransferase (PC

pmc-10542113.title: Relapse of Low Back Pain After Internal Lumbar Fixation Was Diagnosed with SAPHO Syndrome: A Case Report
pmc-10542113.creator: Yanfeng Zhang, Yujia Luo, Yachao Ruan, Xiang Qian, Zhiying Feng
pmc-10542113.description: IntroductionEarly diagnosis of SAPHO syndrome is easily confused with other common spine-related diseases and infections. There is currently no consensus regarding the diagnosis of SAPHO syndrome, and specific treatments are empirical because of its rarity.Case PresentationA 62-year-old woman was referred to our department with complaints of low back and lower extremity pain for 2 years, 1.

pmc-10695668.title: Perioperative Ultrasound-Guided Continuous Caudal Epidural Analgesia in Newborns: A Case Series in a Tertiary Medical Center
pmc-10695668.creator: Filipa Portela, Gabriela Costa, Teresa Cenicante
pmc-10695668.description: BackgroundCaudal epidural anesthesia technique is a relevant method for postoperative analgesia in newborns, allowing for the reduction of drug-induced respiratory depression. The threading of a catheter is, however, uncommon in clinical practice. Our main purpose was to describe our experience regarding caudally inserted epidural catheters in neonates undergoing major abdominal surgery.

pmc-10704702.title: High-grade HER2-positive mucoepidermoid carcinoma of the breast: a case report and review of the literature
pmc-10704702.creator: Mario Della Mura, Céline Clement, Maria P. Foschini, Sara Vander Borght, Lise Waumans, Peter Van Eyken, Esther Hauben, Machteld Keupers, Caroline Weltens, Ann Smeets, Ines Nevelsteen, Giuseppe Floris
pmc-10704702.description: BackgroundMucoepidermoid carcinoma of the breast is a rare special type of salivary gland-like tumor of the breast, usually displaying triple-negative phenotype. To date, only 64 cases have been reported in the English literature. Herein, we report the first case of mucoepidermoid carcinoma of the breast with human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 gene amplification.

pmc-11548305.title: TRPV4—A Multifunctional Cellular Sensor Protein with Therapeutic Potential
pmc-11548305.creator: Sanna Koskimäki, Sari Tojkander
pmc-11548305.description: Transient receptor potential vanilloid (TRPV) channel proteins belong to the superfamily of TRP proteins that form cationic channels in the animal cell membranes. These proteins have various subtype-specific functions, serving, for example, as sensors for pain, pressure, pH, and mechanical extracellular stimuli.

pmc-11591769.title: Managing Crohn’s Disease Postoperative Recurrence Beyond Prophylaxis: A Comprehensive Review with Meta-Analysis
pmc-11591769.creator: Andrei Ovidiu Olteanu, Artsiom Klimko, Eugen Nicolae Tieranu, Andreea Daniela Bota, Carmen Monica Preda, Ioana Tieranu, Christopher Pavel, Mihai Radu Pahomeanu, Cristian Valentin Toma, Adrian Saftoiu, Elena Mirela Ionescu, Cristian George Tieranu
pmc-11591769.description: Background and Aims: Postoperative recurrence in Crohn’s disease remains a significant clinical challenge, with high recurrence rates despite advancements in medical therapy. This study aims to evaluate the efficacy of various treatments for managing postoperative recurrence following ileocolonic resection in Crohn’s disease.

pmc-11599318.title: Fractures of the thoracolumbar spine in osteoporosis
pmc-11599318.creator: Radko Komadina, Frank W Bloemers, Marko Jug, Klaus W Wendt, Christoph Nau, Hans-Christoph Pape
pmc-11599318.description: Due to increasing life expectancy, the prevalence of fractures caused by osteoporosis is raising. These fractures significantly reduce the quality of life in the elderly population. They represent both a disease and an injury simultaneously. While they were once treated solely with conservative methods, new techniques and implants are expanding the indications for surgical treatment.

pmc-11643675.title: Quercetin Reduced and Stabilized Gold Nanoparticle/Al3+: A Rapid, Sensitive Optical Detection Nanoplatform for Fluoride Ion
pmc-11643675.creator: Titilope John Jayeoye, Roselina Panghiyangani, Sudarshan Singh, Nongnuj Muangsin
pmc-11643675.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). In this contribution, facile synthesis of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) at ambient conditions is reported based on the use of the polyphenolic compound quercetin (QT) as the reducing and stabilizing agent at room temperature (RT). Under alkali-induced pH adjustment of QT solution and stirring conditions at RT, QT could quickly reduce gold salt (Au3+) into its nanoparticle form (Au0), resulting in the formation of a sparkling red color colloidal solution (AuNPs) with an absorption maximum at 520 nm.

pmc-11713291.title: Late onset Alzheimer’s Disease mouse model with altered synaptic and behavior phenotypes
pmc-11713291.creator: Ankit Seth, Jacob Bradford Miller, Ashiq M. Rafiq, Ferenc Deak
pmc-11713291.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundGenetically modified mouse models have provided a vital understanding of the Alzheimer’s disease (AD) mechanisms, but these models were generally focused on familial AD and do not recapitulate the late‐onset human AD pathophysiology.

pmc-12433866.title: From mechanisms to therapies: current advances breakthroughs in alopecia areata immunopathology
pmc-12433866.creator: Huai-Bo Zhao, Ya-Nan Zhang, Yan Qiang, Guo-Mi Wang, Li-Wei Wang, Wen-Cheng Jiang, Xi Chen
pmc-12433866.description: Alopecia areata (AA) is a prevalent autoimmune condition characterized by hair loss, with the collapse of hair follicle immune privilege being a pivotal event in its pathogenesis. This collapse involves intricate immunological disturbances, where CD8+NKG2D+ T cells, driven by inflammatory cytokines like IFN-γ, attack hair follicles.

pmc-12524924.title: Emerging Therapeutic and Inflammation Biomarkers: The Role of Meteorin-Like (Metrnl) and Follistatin-Like 1 (FSTL1) in Inflammatory Diseases
pmc-12524924.creator: Tsvetelina Velikova, Konstantina Bakopoulou, Milena Gulinac, Evelina Manova, Hristo Valkov, Dimitrina Miteva, Russka Shumnalieva, Mariapaola Marino
pmc-12524924.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In recent years, Meteorin-like protein (Metrnl/IL-41) and Follistatin-like 1 (FSTL1) have emerged as multifunctional molecules that play roles in immunity, metabolism and tissue remodeling. Although they demonstrate pleiotropic effects, they are promising candidates for biomarkers and possible therapeutic targets. The development of new, disease-specific biomarkers will enable clinicians to more effectively monitor inflammatory activity, more accurately assess disease severity, better predict survival, and select appropriate medical treatments.

pmc-12607636.title: The Influence of Different Light Spectra on Broiler Chicken Endocrine Systems and Productivity
pmc-12607636.creator: Lenuța Galan, Gheorghe Solcan, Carmen Solcan, George K Symeon, Vassilios Dotas
pmc-12607636.description: Simple SummaryLight plays a crucial role in regulating physiological processes in broiler chickens. It not only helps birds see but also reaches deep into their brains, influencing important body functions. In broiler chickens, different LED light colors (e.g., green and blue) can affect the hormone systems that control growth, metabolism, and stress.

pmc-12608138.title: Effect of Energy-Dependent Proton Irradiation in Thin-Film YBa2Cu3O7−δ Superconductor
pmc-12608138.creator: Trevor Harrison, Joshua Kim, Katharina Cook, Hope Weeda, Joseph Fogt, Nolan Miles, Kyuil Cho
pmc-12608138.description: The superconducting properties of YBa2Cu3O7−δ thin films were investigated by conducting 1.7 MeV proton irradiations with a total fluence of 2.64×1017 p/cm2. The superconducting critical temperature (Tc) was reduced from 89.4 K to 10.1 K. The experimental procedure was similar to a previous study (0.6 MeV proton irradiation).

pmc-12659525.title: Patient reported barriers and facilitators of chronic kidney disease care in Sub-Saharan Africa: a mixed methods systematic review using the COM-B model
pmc-12659525.creator: Habtamu Abera Areri, Leul Derbie Ketaw, Hailemariam Berhe, Moses Mwangi Gitonga, Samuel Kimani, Jacob Kariuki, Lisa Thompson, Rebecca Gary
pmc-12659525.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIn Sub-Saharan Africa (SSA), the prevalence of chronic kidney disease (CKD) is on the rise. Treatment for CKD in SSA is characterized by delayed initiation, early discontinuation, inadequate duration of therapy, and suboptimal follow-up.

pmc-13056563.title: Spatio-temporal dynamics of Hendra virus in Australia reveal stable maintenance of diverse viral clades among Pteropus bats
pmc-13056563.creator: Claude Kwe Yinda, John-Sebastian Eden, Erica T Prates, Anna Vlot, Sarah van Tol, Sarah L Anzick, Jianning Wang, Kim Halpin, Benny Borremans, Tamika J Lunn, Kent Barbian, Brown Bulloch, Benjamin Greene, Kimberly Meade-White, Trenton Bushmaker, Caylee A Falvo, Daniel E Crowley, Devin N Jones-Slobodian
pmc-13056563.description: Hendra virus (HeV) was discovered in 1994 in Australia. Limited genomic data have hindered comprehensive understanding of HeV’s evolutionary dynamics. Here we recovered 48 HeV genomes from bats and 9 from horses from Australia between 2016 and 2020, revealing four distinct clades.

pmc-13225246.title: Chronic widespread pain and the risk of cardiovascular disease-a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13225246.creator: Ann-Sofie Rönnegård, Tessa Schillemans, Björn Äng, Katja Boersma, Johan Ärnlöv, Elena Tseli
pmc-13225246.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Supplemental Digital Content is Available in the Text. Introduction Recent research suggests a close link between 2 of the world's major health conditions: pain and cardiovascular disease. Pain 1 year after a myocardial infarction seems to be a stronger risk factor for mortality than smoking,7 and previous research has suggested an association between chronic pain, defined as pain >3 months, and cardiovascular disease.18 Among individuals with chronic pain, those with chronic widespread pain (CWP) seem to be at the highest risk of

pmc-13425965.title: Extreme hyperleukocytosis and blueberry muffin skin lesions as the initial presentation of neonatal leukemia: a case report
pmc-13425965.creator: Marina A Bustamante-Ordoñez, Michele A Macavilca-Toribio, Judith R Arenas-Vasquez, Victor Roman-Lazarte, Carlos Zavaleta-Corvera, Ángel Samanez-Obeso
pmc-13425965.description: BackgroundNeonatal leukemia is a rare and aggressive hematologic malignancy, accounting for less than 1% of pediatric leukemias. Mixed phenotype acute leukemia (MPAL) is particularly uncommon in this age group and poses significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. Hyperleukocytosis and leukostasis are life-threatening complications requiring urgent intervention.

pmc-13523209.title: Prevalence and predictors of potentially inappropriate medication use among older adults with heart failure: a 2023 beers criteria–based evaluation
pmc-13523209.creator: Marwan Sheikh-Taha

pmc-13563054.title: Vitamin D Level and Antibody Response to the BBIBP‐CorV Vaccine in Pregnant Women
pmc-13563054.creator: Shahab Falahi, Mahdi Vahabi, Hojjat Sayyadi, Azra Kenarkoohi
pmc-13563054.description: Background and AimsSeveral factors influence the response to the vaccine, including age, gender, pregnancy, microbiota composition, immune function, sex hormones, and micronutrients (such as vitamin D). This study aimed to evaluate antibody responses induced by the BBIBP‐CorV vaccine in pregnant women and investigate its association with serum vitamin D levels.

pmc-13607866.title: Unilateral Versus Bilateral Percutaneous Kyphoplasty for Single-Level Thoracolumbar Osteoporotic Vertebral Compression Fractures: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
pmc-13607866.creator: Panagiotis Korovessis, Vasileios Syrimpeis, Georgios Vlachopoulos, Dimitrios Ntourantonis, George Sakellaropoulos
pmc-13607866.description: Background/Objectives: The optimal surgical approach for Percutaneous KyphoPlasty (PKP) in patients with recent single-level Osteoporotic Vertebral Compression Fractures (OVCFs) remains controversial. Most available previous meta-analyses included studies with variable heterogeneity, often mixing unilateral and bilateral MIS approaches, differing surgical techniques, and various fracture patterns, which limited the reliability of their conclusions.

pmc-13668696.title: 7-ketocholesterol contributes to microglia-driven increases in astrocyte reactive oxygen species in a mouse model of Alzheimer’s disease
pmc-13668696.creator: Kayalvizhi Radhakrishnan, Yiyu Zhang, Oluwaseun Mustapha, Thaddeus K Weigel, Clint M Upchurch, Xiaodong Tian, Franklin Herbert, Wenyuan Huang, Norbert Leitinger, Ukpong B Eyo, Huiwang Ai, Heather A Ferris
pmc-13668696.description: Oxidative stress is a prominent feature of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Within this context, cholesterol undergoes oxidation, producing the pro-inflammatory product 7-ketocholesterol (7-KC). In this study, we observe elevated levels of 7-KC in the brains of the 3xTg mouse model of AD.

pmc-13685770.title: An advanced LLM-powered article extraction pipeline delivers a database of buffers for protein studies and protein expression conditions
pmc-13685770.creator: Zhuojian Chen, Eng Aloysius, J Sivaraman
pmc-13685770.description: Optimizing protein expression and buffer conditions is a major challenge in life-science research and biotechnology. We present an LLM-powered extraction pipeline that systematically converts unstructured scientific literature into a structured, queryable database. Leveraging advanced optical character recognition, custom reranker models, and large language models, our system achieves ~97% extraction accuracy.
